FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
The THC inference of 5 nanograms per milliliter of blood applies to DUI only; DWAI has no THC inference level at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group drug impairment; difficulty three; confusable sec03-F04 vs sec03-F05. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A01
For alcohol, BAC roughly reflects impairment, but for marijuana the measured THC level does not, which is why behavior evidence matters so much. [A01]
Why it matters: group drug impairment; difficulty two; prereq sec03-F03. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
Refusing a chemical test brings two different time periods: one year of revocation and two years of ignition interlock use. [A01]
Why it matters: group express consent; difficulty three; confusable sec03-F11 vs sec03-F13. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
Penalties from the same incident do not run at the same time as the refusal revocation; they are added onto its end. [A01]
Why it matters: group express consent; difficulty two; prereq sec03-F11. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A01
The earphone ban covers devices on both ears, so a single-ear wireless device and hearing aids remain legal. [A01]
Why it matters: group fitness to drive; difficulty two; confusable sec03-F20 vs sec03-F21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A01
The eye exam advice is every year or two, while the fatigue advice is to break long drives into two-hour segments; do not swap these intervals. [A01]
Why it matters: group fitness to drive; difficulty one; confusable sec03-F17 vs sec03-F22. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A01
Express consent covers blood, breath, saliva and urine tests, not only a breath test. [A01]
Why it matters: group express consent; difficulty one; prereq sec03-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

Misconception: a low THC reading means you are fit to drive; impairment and THC level are not linked. [A01]
Misconception: you can negotiate a drunk-driving charge down to a lesser offense in Colorado; plea bargaining out of it is not allowed. [A01]
Misconception: any headset is fine if the music is quiet; covering both ears is prohibited whatever the volume. [A01]
Mnemonic: Refuse once, lose for one, blow for two, meaning revocation then interlock years. [A01]
Glossary: Express consent means agreeing in advance, by driving, to chemical testing. [A01]
Glossary: Ignition interlock means a breath-testing device that blocks the engine when alcohol is detected. [A01]
Glossary: Polydrug impairment means impairment from two or more substances used together. [A01]
Glossary: Permissible inference means a level from which a court may infer impairment unless other evidence shows otherwise. [A01]
